revisionNote: 2026-10-26: two deliberate changes. (1) The particle layer was toned down (fewer visible dust specks, matched to the reference frame), so the canonical-capture baselines for frame, top background, category icon row and item label row were re-measured on the current feature build: frame 18.02/0.8301, top background 20.24/0.9344, category icon row 21.05/0.8950, item label row 11.94/0.3910; clock and info bar are unchanged. (2) The Game column was reshaped: Steam Store, then one All Games folder (detail = distinct Steam titles, 282), then the dev_flash utilities. The inline installed rows and the top-level Not Installed row are gone; Not Installed is now reached through All Games (folder mode library, 275 rows). The named-state recipes and their self-baseline references were refreshed for that shape. The stored-pair baselines above remain the historical RPCS3 comparison numbers and are unchanged. (3) The clock now defaults to the American format the user asked for (MM/DD date, 12-hour time, one space), so the canonical clock text and info bar no longer match the DD/MM 24-hour RPCS3 reference frame by design: their captureBaseline is re-measured at 11.39/0.4105 and 14.78/0.6117. Switching clock/dateFormat and clock/hourFormat back to DD/MM + 24-hour reproduces the reference string and scores 13.61/0.6226 and 17.21/0.7114.

baselinePair.note: Stored 1920x1080 native capture of the settled Game root menu, scored against the stored RPCS3 frame. This pair is the historical baseline: whole frame 18.20 dB / 0.8388 SSIM. Offline scoring of this pair is deterministic, so its gate catches tooling (decoder/metric/crop) regressions.

tolerance.rationale: Two canonical capture runs are pixel-identical (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000), so run-to-run jitter contributes nothing. The budget therefore only absorbs GPU/driver shader noise and small environment drift. 0.5 dB PSNR is a 12% MSE increase, while a visible layer regression (a moved icon, a dropped label row, a shifted gradient) moves a layer score by more than 1 dB; 0.004 SSIM is likewise far above observed noise and far below a visible regression.

capture.note: Canonical capture recipe. All animation clocks are pinned, so two runs are pixel-identical. XMB_STEAM_ROOT points at an empty directory: the stored RPCS3 reference frame's Game column predates this PC's Steam library and shows the dev_flash XMBML entries only. backgroundClock 10:00 is the traced daytime mapping used by the stored baseline; uiClock matches the reference frame's 25/10 12:32. The default exe is the feature build that carries the reshaped Game column and the toned-down particles; pass --exe when the integration build moves.

stateSelfBaseline.rationale: Named states have no RPCS3 frame: their reference is the deterministic native render itself, so a fresh capture must reproduce that frame (self-baseline regression gate, not firmware fidelity). Two runs of every state are byte-identical on this machine (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000). 55 dB still catches any deterministic drawing change (one changed 255-level pixel already costs ~68 dB on a 1080p frame) while leaving room for GPU/driver shader noise; 0.9995 SSIM is the same margin. Refresh a reference deliberately after an intended rendering or layout change with --states --save-reference.
